subject.title: Feature request: Local plugin scanner CLI for pre-publish validation

question: Should ClawHub adopt ClawScan as a component for the supported pre-publish plugin workflow, and what local-versus-hosted validation contract should that workflow guarantee?
rationale: The code proves several viable partial implementations, but choosing the authoritative public boundary requires maintainer intent about privacy, credentials, hosted parity, versioning, and long-term scanner compatibility.

options.title: Adopt with ClawHub adapter
options.body: Compose ClawScan static findings with ClawHub package and manifest validation, explicitly marking model-backed or registry-only checks as hosted-only.

options.title: Build ClawHub-native scanner
options.body: Maintain the full pre-publish scanner and all compatibility guarantees directly in the ClawHub CLI and backend.

options.title: Keep separate tools
options.body: Document `package validate`, repository tooling, and external ClawScan as independent surfaces without promising one authoritative pre-publish result.

recommendation.title: Adopt with ClawHub adapter
recommendation.body: Compose ClawScan static findings with ClawHub package and manifest validation, explicitly marking model-backed or registry-only checks as hosted-only.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the closest merged implementation and have the strongest recent history across the affected scanner and validation surfaces.
